title: How to Prepare for the Dangote Refinery IPO
summary: The Dangote Refinery IPO hits the NGX in September 14, 2026. Here is everything investors need to know to prepare before the subscription window opens.
body_markdown:
**In short:** The Dangote Refinery IPO has been approved, with a subscription window of 14 September to 13 October 2026 at a fixed ₦525 per share (minimum 10 shares, ₦5,250). To be ready, open and fund a Bamboo account, confirm your CSCS number, decide how much you can afford to invest, and read the prospectus when it is published. Only invest money you can afford to lose. This is general information, not advice.


Africa’s largest refinery is about to become a publicly listed company, and Nigerian investors now have a firm, short window to get ready. The Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals IPO has been approved by the Securities and Exchange Commission, and the subscription window runs from 14 September to 13 October 2026. This is no longer a distant prospect. The terms are set, and the clock is running.


This guide covers what the IPO is, what makes it unusual, the confirmed timeline, and the practical steps to position yourself before the window closes. For the full application walkthrough, see our companion guide,[how to buy Dangote Refinery IPO shares](https://learn.investbamboo.com/how-to-buy-dangote-refinery-ipo-shares-in-nigeria-a-step-by-step-guide/) . This is general information, not investment advice.


## What has been confirmed


Following SEC approval and the signing ceremony on 7 September 2026, the offer’s headline terms are set:


- **Price:** ₦525.00 per share, at a fixed price
- **Shares on offer:** 4.1 billion ordinary shares
- **Minimum application:** 10 shares (₦5,250)
- **Subscription window:** 14 September to 13 October 2026
- **Potential size:** about ₦2.15 trillion if fully subscribed
- **Listing:** on the Main Board of the[Nigerian Exchange](https://ngxgroup.com/) after the offer closes


One thing to note: the full prospectus, the detailed document with the audited financials and exact dividend terms, is expected to be published before the window opens. Our guide on[what the prospectus will tell you](https://learn.investbamboo.com/what-the-dangote-refinery-ipo-prospectus-will-tell-you-and-what-to-look-for-before-you-invest/) covers what to look for in it.


## What is the Dangote Refinery IPO?


The IPO is the offering of shares in Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals to the public on the Nigerian Exchange. The refinery is already operational: located in the Ibeju-Lekki Free Zone outside Lagos, it processes 650,000 barrels of crude per day, making it the world’s largest single-train refinery, and it cost around $20 billion to build. It supplies a large share of Nigeria’s petrol demand and exports refined fuel to other African countries. When the offer completes, Nigerian and other investors will be able to own a piece of that infrastructure directly.


Analysts have valued the refinery at around $40 billion or more. This offer of 4.1 billion shares at ₦525 would raise roughly ₦2.15 trillion, about $1.5 billion, if fully subscribed, putting it on track to be one of the largest equity offerings in Nigerian and African history. The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited holds a minority stake in the refinery, taken during construction, which is not part of this offer.


## What makes this IPO different?


### The proposed dollar dividend


The most distinctive feature is the proposed dividend structure: investors buy shares in naira, but would have the option to receive dividends in US dollars, supported by the refinery’s foreign-currency export earnings. For investors who have watched the naira weaken, the idea of earning hard-currency income from a naira-priced investment is a notable draw. Its exact terms and regulatory status will be set out in the prospectus, so treat it as proposed until you can confirm it there. Our guide on[how naira devaluation and inflation affect your investments](https://learn.investbamboo.com/how-naira-devaluation-and-inflation-affect-your-investments/) explains why dollar exposure appeals to many Nigerian investors, and why it is never a one-way bet.


### Pan-African listing ambitions


While the NGX is the immediate focus, the group has signalled ambitions for listings across multiple African exchanges over time, which could eventually let investors in other markets access the stock locally.


### A business already in operation


Unlike an IPO where you buy into future potential, this refinery is already producing at scale, generating revenue and supplying the market. That does not remove risk, but the risk profile differs from a pre-revenue listing: you are buying into an operating business, not a promise.


## The confirmed timeline


The old speculative timeline is settled. Here is what is confirmed:


- **7 September 2026:** SEC approval and signing ceremony, headline terms confirmed
- **Before the window opens:** full prospectus expected to be published
- **14 September to 13 October 2026:** subscription window open
- **After the offer closes:** allotment, refunds where applications exceed supply, and listing on the NGX Main Board


The window is short and firm, and IPO windows do not extend because demand is high. Preparing now, rather than in the final days, is what separates investors who get in from those who miss out.


## How to prepare: a step-by-step guide


### Step 1: Open and fund an account


To apply, you need an account with a SEC-registered platform connected to the NGX. If you do not have one,[download the Bamboo app](https://onelink.to/investbamboo) and onboard with a valid ID and your BVN. Then fund your account by bank transfer ahead of 14 September, since payment is due in full on application. On Bamboo, there are no fees to apply for this IPO, so the amount you need is exactly the number of shares multiplied by ₦525.


### Step 2: Confirm your CSCS number


Every NGX investor needs a Central Securities Clearing System account, which holds your shares. On Bamboo, this is created automatically when you open your Nigerian stocks account. Confirm your CSCS number in the app before the window opens, since applications without a valid one cannot be processed.


### Step 3: Decide how much you can afford


Before the window opens, decide your amount, and decide it on the right basis. Only invest money you can afford to leave tied up for several weeks and, ultimately, money you can afford to lose. Never borrow to invest, because a loan’s repayment stays fixed whatever the shares do. Keep any single IPO to a share of your portfolio you are comfortable with, rather than overcommitting to the excitement of a big listing. Our guide on[how much you need to invest in the Dangote Refinery IPO](https://learn.investbamboo.com/how-much-do-you-need-to-invest-in-an-ipo-2/) works through sizing and the cost at different application amounts.


### Step 4: Read the prospectus when it is published


The prospectus is the legal document containing the audited financials, the exact dividend terms, the risk factors, and the full offer terms. When it is published, expected before the window opens, read it rather than relying on media summaries. Our guide on[what the prospectus will tell you](https://learn.investbamboo.com/what-the-dangote-refinery-ipo-prospectus-will-tell-you-and-what-to-look-for-before-you-invest/) shows exactly what to look for.


### Step 5: Apply when the window opens


From 14 September, the offer appears in the Nigerian stocks section of the Bamboo app. Select it, enter your number of shares, review the total, and submit. Because high-profile offers are often oversubscribed, you may be allotted fewer shares than you applied for, with the balance refunded. Our guides on[what happens when the IPO is oversubscribed](https://learn.investbamboo.com/what-happens-if-the-dangote-ipo-is-oversubscribed-understanding-ipo-demand-in-nigeria/) and[how long allotment takes](https://learn.investbamboo.com/how-long-does-public-offer-allotment-take-in-nigeria/) explain what to expect afterward.


## Key risks to understand


Preparing well also means being honest about the risks.


The proposed dollar dividend is a key part of the appeal, and its exact terms and regulatory status will be confirmed in the prospectus. Do not assume the structure until you can see it there. A high-profile listing can also carry a valuation premium, where the initial price reflects strong demand as much as conservative fundamentals, so short-term price movement after listing can be volatile. Adding the refinery to a portfolio already weighted toward Nigeria increases your concentration in one country and the energy sector. And the plan to expand capacity toward 1.4 million barrels per day is a significant execution challenge, where delays or cost overruns could affect profitability. None of these is a reason to avoid the offer outright. Each is a reason to read the prospectus carefully and size your investment sensibly.


## Why this IPO matters


Beyond the transaction, a successful listing of this scale would show that Nigeria can channel domestic and international capital into its most strategic infrastructure through public markets, and it could bring a new generation of retail investors into the NGX. For individual investors, it offers the chance to own a piece of a facility that has become central to the national conversation about what Nigeria can build at world-class scale. Whether it belongs in your portfolio, though, is a decision only you can make, based on the prospectus and your own circumstances.


## Frequently asked questions


**When does the Dangote Refinery IPO open?** The subscription window runs from 14 September to 13 October 2026, following SEC approval and the confirmation of terms at the 7 September signing ceremony.


**How do I prepare for the IPO?** Open and fund an account with a SEC-registered platform such as Bamboo, confirm your CSCS number, decide how much you can afford to invest, and read the prospectus when it is published. Do this before the window opens, not during it.


**How much do I need to invest?** The minimum is 10 shares at ₦525 each, which is ₦5,250. On Bamboo there are no fees to apply, so that is the full cost of the minimum. Our dedicated guide covers larger amounts.


**Has the prospectus been published?** The offer has been approved and its terms confirmed, but the full prospectus document has not yet been made publicly available. It is expected before the subscription window opens.


**Is the dollar dividend confirmed?** The dollar dividend has been proposed, and its exact terms and regulatory status will be set out in the prospectus. Confirm the details there before relying on it.
